label: Ankle injury right after being fouled
explain: Fouled and sent to the line. The foul means contact on the play, such as a hard foul on a drive or a landing on a defender's foot, though the play-by-play can't say which. Holds up in every check, but only for ankles: for other injuries it doesn't survive the toughest check.

label: Any injury right after a steal by the player
explain: Fits the sprint, finish or scramble after the steal. Holds up in every check, counting all kinds of injury together; most kinds lean the same way, though not head injuries.

label: Hand, wrist, finger or arm injury after the other team attacked the rim
explain: The player was on defense for a layup, dunk or tip-in. Fits contesting or swiping at the ball, though the play-by-play doesn't say who contested it. Clear only for hand and arm injuries, and based on fewer cases.

label: Pulled muscle or Achilles injury right after a drive or cut to the basket
explain: Fits injuries from pushing off and accelerating. Points the same way in every check, but only just clears the bar for the many plays we tested: worth checking on film.

label: Ankle injury right after a rebound
explain: Landing from a rebound is a well-known cause of ankle sprains. Here it leans the same way but isn't proven: the play-by-play only credits the player who gets the rebound, not everyone who went up for it.
